memo.verdict: A 15-unit to 16-unit mixed-use building is realistically achievable under an approved site plan valid through April 2027, but the project is not worth pursuing at the $475,000 asking price based on negative supportable land value projections.
memo.as_of_right: CD-5 zoning allows mixed-use multifamily as-of-right under Table 345.405.A-6. The 2,235 sq ft lot permits 100% coverage and 6 stories (approx 80 ft max height), yielding 13,410 gross sq ft. Deducting ground-floor retail leaves 11,175 gross residential sq ft, capping density at 15 to 16 units. Parking requires 1 space per unit plus 0.25 per bedroom over 1 under Table 345.405.N-1, with a 100% buyout option at $30,000 per space for small lots under Sec 345-405N(1)(h). Projects with 10 or more units require a 10% AFFH set-aside at 60% AMI under Sec 345-405.U.
memo.approval_path: Existing approval. The Planning Commission approved the site plan on April 25, 2022, and Local Law I-14 of 2025 extended approval through April 25, 2027. Time and entitlement risk are low if built as approved, but construction must vest before expiration.
legal_issues: Verification of approved site plan expiration date through April 25, 2027.
Unstated additional parking buyout and GEIS fair share mitigation fee amounts owed by the buyer.
Discrepancy in approved unit count between 15 units in Board of Trustees records and 16 units in AKRF review files.
Compliance with mandatory 50-year 10% AFFH affordable set-aside covenant at 60% AMI under Sec 345-405.U.
Floodplain compliance requirements and insurance costs due to FEMA Zone AE designation.
memo.test_fit: The building envelope is capped by a 2,235 sq ft footprint (100% coverage on 29 ft by 72 ft lot) and 6 stories. Total gross area is 13,410 sq ft, featuring 691 sq ft of ground-floor retail and 5 upper residential floors. The unit count ranges from 15 to 16 units (5 studios and 10-11 one-bedrooms). Tiny lot area and the 6-story height ceiling limit density first, not parking or FAR.
memo.value: Land cost at the $475,000 asking price is $31,667 per buildable unit for the 15-unit approved plan ($29,688 per unit if 16 units). A second analyst's pro forma estimates a maximum supportable land value of -$2,618,510 based on $450/sq ft hard costs and a 4.24% yield on cost, showing the ask exceeds supportable value.
diligence: Confirm site plan approval extension to April 25, 2027, in writing with the Village.
Clarify exact approved unit count (15 vs 16 units) from the stamped site plan set.
Obtain exact dollar figures for required parking buyout fees and GEIS fair share mitigation payments.
Verify building flood-proofing requirements and quotes for FEMA Zone AE flood insurance.
Confirm lot size of 2,235 sq ft and 29 ft frontage via a current boundary survey.
memo.enablers: CD-5 district as-of-right multifamily use, 100% lot coverage allowance, small-lot parking buyout up to 100% at $30,000 per space under Sec 345-405N(1)(h), and CD-5 Public Parking Incentive Zoning under Sec 345-405X.
memo.highest_and_best_use: Not enough data. FACTS lack verified local market rent comps, sale prices, and land comps (the second analyst relied on proxy rents from New Rochelle). Based strictly on zoning approvals, the highest density use is the approved 6-story mixed-use building with 15-16 apartments and ground-floor commercial.

memo.verdict: The site realistically accommodates an 11-unit market-rate or 13- to 16-unit affordable multifamily building as of right, but a second analyst estimates negative supportable land value at the $999,000 ask.
memo.as_of_right: Multifamily development is permitted as of right in the R7-1 district. On this 2,800 square foot lot, standard residential FAR is 3.44, generating 9,632 square feet of floor area and 10 to 14 units (roughly 11 units at 900 gross square feet per unit). Universal Affordability Preference (UAP) increases FAR to 4.13 (11,558 square feet, ~13 units). Qualifying affordable housing allows FAR 5.01 (14,028 square feet, 15 to 20 units, ~16 units) under ZR 23-22. Off-street parking is waived to 0 spaces under ZR 25-232 because the calculated requirement does not exceed 10 spaces.
memo.approval_path: As-of-right development. Standard and UAP multifamily developments require standard Department of Buildings plan examination without discretionary land-use approvals. This minimizes approval time and land-use risk. Expanding to the qualifying affordable FAR of 5.01 requires executing a regulatory agreement with HPD or HDC.
legal_issues: Vacant delivery and demolition clearance for the existing 1920 single-family home.
Affordability covenant compliance under HPD or HDC if using UAP (maximum 60 percent AMI average) or qualifying FAR 5.01.
Street width classification on Harrison Avenue (60 feet, narrow street), which caps standard building height at 75 feet.
memo.test_fit: The building footprint is capped at 1,900 square feet after accounting for the mandatory 30-foot rear yard, staying within the 80 percent lot coverage limit. Standard narrow-street height allows a 65-foot base and 75-foot max height (about 7 floors). Qualifying affordable height permits an 85-foot base and 105-foot max height (about 10 floors). Floor area ratio is the primary binding limit on density. Unit count ranges from 10 to 14 units standard (~11 units) up to 15 to 20 units under affordable programs (~13 to 16 units). Parking requirement is 0 spaces.
memo.value: At the $999,000 ask, land cost is $104 per buildable square foot and $71,357 to $99,900 per unit for the standard tier. With UAP or qualifying affordable bonus floor area, land cost drops to $71 per buildable square foot and $49,950 to $66,600 per unit. Recent Bronx development land comps trade between $89 and $168 per buildable square foot (such as 2449 Grand Avenue at $89 per buildable square foot and $60,417 per unit). A second analyst's pro forma estimates maximum supportable land value at negative $1,252,000 for conventional and negative $2,414,090 for affordable tracks.
diligence: Review the broker-offered survey to verify lot boundaries, 30-foot frontage, and 2,800 square foot area.
Confirm vacant delivery status and obtain municipal records for the existing 1-family structure.
Conduct a Phase I Environmental Site Assessment.
Verify HPD and HDC regulatory agreement terms and 485-x program eligibility requirements if pursuing UAP or qualifying FAR.
memo.enablers: The Universal Affordability Preference (UAP) under ZR Chapter 27 permits a 20 percent bonus to FAR 4.13 (~13 units) with bonus space kept permanently affordable at an average of 60 percent AMI or below. A qualifying affordable project under an HPD or HDC regulatory agreement can reach FAR 5.01 (~16 units) utilizing LIHTC and 485-x tax incentives.
memo.highest_and_best_use: Multifamily rental is the indicated use based on local rental comps (The Bronx Vibe rents at $2,580 for studios, $2,895 for 1BRs, and $3,300 for 2BRs). Building an 11-unit conventional rental avoids regulatory caps, whereas building 13 to 16 units depends on securing 485-x or LIHTC financing to offset affordable rent restrictions. A second analyst estimates conventional rental yields a better net operating income ($231,660), though both tracks fail financial hurdles at the current ask.

memo.verdict: A 5-story mixed-use building with 1 commercial space and 5 residential units can be built as of right, but the deal is not worth pursuing at the $699,000 asking price.
memo.as_of_right: Zone NC-1 permits mixed-use buildings with ground-floor commercial and residential above up to 5 stories and 55 feet. The 2,379 SF lot requires a 15 percent rear yard setback, leaving a footprint of approximately 2,022 SF. Across 4 upper residential floors, this provides roughly 8,088 SF of gross residential area, yielding 5 units at 1,400 SF each. Lots under 5,000 SF require zero off-street parking spaces.
memo.approval_path: As-of-right site plan review. This requires standard administrative site plan approval without variances, minimizing entitlement risk and review time.
legal_issues: Full text of Sec 345-46 was unreadable due to online access blocks, leaving lot coverage parameters unconfirmed.
No prior approvals exist for this lot in official city records.
The 2,379 SF lot area is below the standard 2,500 SF minimum, requiring verification as a lawful existing lot of record under Sec 345-46E.1.
memo.test_fit: The site envelope allows a 5-story, 55-foot building with 0 ft front and side yards and a 15 percent rear yard setback. Building footprint is 2,022 SF with a maximum gross envelope of 10,110 SF over 5 stories. The site allows 1 commercial space on the ground floor and up to 5 residential units above. Density is limited by lot size and height limits rather than parking, as zero parking is required.
memo.value: At the $699,000 asking price, the land cost is $139,800 per buildable unit for a 5-unit program. A nearby land comp at 414-432 Hoboken Ave traded at $49,618 per unit. A second analyst estimate projects total development costs of $6,069,938 and a yield on cost of 2.37 percent, concluding a negative supportable land value at current pricing.

memo.approval_path: Development of the 4,952 buildable SF multi-family scheme is as-of-right with standard plan review, carrying low time and entitlement risk. Subdividing the lot or adding a second detached residence will require local site plan and lot split approvals.

method:
BOUNTY feasibility memos: land-use attorney + architect review for every listed site
and the strongest off-market targets.

Two layers, kept separate on purpose:
  1. FACTS AND MATH (deterministic): parcel data from the official GIS (NYC MapPLUTO,
     Westchester County parcels), street frontage measured edge by edge, the zoning
     district's floor area (NYC ZR 23-22 standard and UAP), verified municipal rules
     (Yonkers Table 43-3 / 43-4: FAR, lot area per unit, coverage, parking), approvals
     with their public sources (bounty/data/feasibility_sites.json).
  2. MEMO (Gemini, free tier, no web access): writes the attorney/architect memo from
     those facts only. It may not add approvals, dates, numbers or programs that are not
     in the facts; anything missing is listed as a diligence item.
